questions.question: If a driver cannot find a student after the student has left the bus, what should the driver do?

options.text: Secure the bus and leave to look for the student.
Assume the student left safely.
Walk to the back of the bus to see if the student got back on.
Ask another student if they have seen the student.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus and leave to look for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find a student after they leave the bus, you must secure the bus and search for the missing student around and underneath the bus.

questions.question: When taking the driving test and asked to make a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use a turn signal since you were told to make the turn.
Check traffic only to your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, you must check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Where are a school bus's danger zones located?

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only at the rear and left side of the bus.
In front, on the sides, and at the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front, on the sides, and at the rear of the bus.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children are most likely to be hit by the bus or another vehicle. These areas are in front, on the sides, and at the rear of the bus. Danger zones extend up to 10 feet from every side of the bus.

questions.question: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing while driving a school bus, what should you do?

options.text: Get ready to go as soon as the train passes.
Ignore the signs and signals.
Open the door to listen and look for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the door to listen and look for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, do not rely only on signals. You must quiet all passengers, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. After a train passes, check for another train coming from either direction before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery roads.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) stop your wheels from locking up on slippery surfaces. ABS helps you stay in control when you brake hard on wet or icy roads. Drive and brake a bus with ABS the same way you would without it.

questions.question: When leaving a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Keep one hand on the handrail at all times.
Move quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep one hand on the handrail at all times.
questions.explanation: When leaving a bus during the skills test, face the bus and keep three points of contact with the handrail at all times. Not following this rule may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: Why should a bus driver stop at least 10 feet away from students waiting at a stop?

options.text: So the students walk to the bus and you can see their movements.
Because buses are hard to drive.
So the students do not get scared of the bus coming toward them.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the students walk to the bus and you can see their movements.
questions.explanation: Stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This makes them walk toward the bus, so you can watch their movements.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a bus driver should:

options.text: Put the bus in park.
Put the bus in first gear.
Put the bus in reverse.
Put the bus in third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the bus in park.
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, put the bus in park. If there is no park gear, use neutral instead.

questions.question: If a bus breaks down on railroad tracks, the driver should:

options.text: Get everyone off the bus and far away from the tracks.
Keep everyone on the bus and try to wave the train down.
Keep everyone on the bus and wait for help.
Keep everyone on the bus and call for a tow truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone off the bus and far away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If a bus breaks down or gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the bus right away with everyone inside. Move everyone far away from the bus at an angle toward where the train is coming from to avoid flying debris.

questions.question: Once you have stopped during the stop/start test, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on the four-way flashers.
Do not use four-way flashers because it is just a test, not an emergency.
Leave the bus in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Once stopped during the stop/start test, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of distortions.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be present and free of cracks, distortions, and rust. They must be tight, not loose. Check that all bolt holes are also free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: When checking tire condition during a vehicle inspection, you should:

options.text: Ensure that the insides of the tires are more worn than the outsides.
Ensure that the outsides of the tires are more worn than the insides.
Ensure that the middles of the tires are more worn than the outsides.
Ensure that the tires have even wear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure that the tires have even wear.
questions.explanation: When checking your tires during a vehicle inspection, make sure the tread is worn evenly across all tires.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during a basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Fail only that exercise.
Lose extra points from your final score.
Automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must always face the vehicle and use three points of contact. If the vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will automatically fail the entire test.

questions.question: When students are picked up by a school bus, they should:

options.text: Wait at a designated bus stop.
Be picked up from anywhere by the driver.
Have parents choose where the bus stop will be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver should pick up and drop off students only at bus stops approved by the school district.

questions.question: After completing a basic vehicle control skills test exercise, your vehicle should be:

options.text: In the general area described by the examiner.
In the exact position described by the examiner.
Within three feet of the position described by the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position described by the examiner.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. Not following instructions exactly may result in failing the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: When loading or unloading passengers, a school bus with no park gear should be placed in:

options.text: Reverse
First gear
Neutral

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral
questions.explanation: When stopping to load or unload students, put a school bus in park if possible. If there is no park gear, put the bus in neutral and set the parking brake.

questions.question: During an emergency, where should students stay?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the bus
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control if they stay on the bus. Only evacuate students if staying on the bus puts them at risk of injury.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Parallel park.
Inspect your tires.
Monitor your gauges.
Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and the bus must be evacuated, students should go to:

options.text: A nearby building
The closest tree
A nearby river
A mountain

questions.correctAnswerText: A nearby building
questions.explanation: If evacuating due to a tornado, lead students to shelter in a nearby building. If no building is available, take them to a ditch or culvert. Avoid areas where water might flood and stay far enough from the bus so it won't land on them if it tips.

questions.question: School bus stops can only be changed by:

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.
Students.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver cannot change a bus stop location without written approval from the school district.
